title: Sequential Learning Algorithms for Contextual Model-Free Influence Maximization

problem.claim: Studies online influence maximization over repeated campaign rounds, where the objective is cumulative new activations and contextual and historical information can inform seed selection.

contributions.claim: Defines Episodic Contextual Influence Maximization with Persistence (ECIMP).
Proposes LSVI-GT-UCB, an optimistic episodic reinforcement-learning algorithm with linear approximation.
Estimates each seed node's remaining potential using a Good-Turing estimator modified by an estimated Q-function.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Empirical comparisons with leading methods on two real-world datasets and one synthetic set favor the proposed algorithm, according to the authors.

narrative_sequence.summary: Frames sequential seed-node selection for cumulative information spread across a multi-round campaign.
Restricts rewards to new activations and uses contextual and historical information for policy learning.
Connects the setting to influencer marketing, persistent first activations, and available side information.
Names ECIMP and proposes LSVI-GT-UCB with Good-Turing potential estimation modified by an estimated Q-function.
Reports comparisons on two real-world datasets and one synthetic dataset.

source_observation.claim: The formulation distinguishes newly activated users from persistent prior activations and uses campaign history and round context.

interpretation.claim: Reward definitions and persistent state can materially shape a sequential influence-maximization policy.

application.claim: When specifying repeated diffusion campaigns, state whether rewards count only new activations and whether prior campaign data informs decisions.

exception.claim: This formulation is specific to campaigns with persistent first activations and available contextual or historical information.

unknowns: The abstract does not report regret bounds or proof details.
It does not name datasets, baselines, metrics, numerical results, or experimental conditions.
